syllabus_extract: Brief introduction to aircraft stability. (Static and dynamic) explanation of longitudinal stability, lateral stability, directional stability
specific_objectives: 14.2.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain the functions of AFCS.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of IB diagrams regarding stability axes; Instructor supervision required for diagram interpretation.
intro_questions: What is the definition of aircraft stability?
List the three primary axes of aircraft motion.
Define the term 'equilibrium' in the context of flight.

development.content:
Static vs Dynamic Stability definitions
Longitudinal stability and CG location
Lateral stability and dihedral effect
Directional stability and vertical fin
Static margin and neutral point

topics: Effect of speed on stability characteristics
development.content:
Restoring moments in longitudinal axis
Rolling moments in lateral axis
Yawing moments in directional axis
Interrelationship of stability axes
Effect of speed on stability characteristics

topics: Role of AFCS in maintaining stability
development.content:
Role of AFCS in maintaining stability
Automatic stabilization mechanisms
Pilot inputs vs automatic corrections
Limitations of AFCS systems
Integration of stability with control

summary_questions: Explain how the vertical fin contributes to directional stability.
Describe the relationship between center of gravity and longitudinal stability.
How does the AFCS assist the pilot in maintaining lateral stability?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on how the concepts of longitudinal, lateral, and directional stability discussed in this lesson will be expanded upon in LP 14 regarding divergence and Dutch roll.

pft_rows.syllabus: Introduction to directional divergence, spiral divergence, Dutch roll and controllability.
